version: LOCK 65 V1 (9 Nov 2026) - the scholar's notebook, chapter 2: Honesty and trade
builds_on: LOCK 3 (page 1, read with Idris), LOCK 34 runner, LOCK 51 (the last page). Every reference checked on sunnah.com; the game never shows the reference.

chapter.title: Honesty and trade
chapter.story: As a young man he sold paper in the markets and was known for weighing ink as carefully as gold.

pages.saying: Part of a person's good Islam is leaving what does not concern him.
pages.idris: Shakir could learn from this page.
pages.found: Umm Hani found a page lining an old hat bought from a pedlar.

pages.saying: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
pages.idris: Would you want the coin that rolled to your foot to come back to you? Then you know.
pages.found: Mukhtar hands you a loaf wrapped in an old page. “Look at the writing on this.”

pages.saying: Your smile at your brother is charity; enjoining good, guiding a lost man and removing a stone from the path are charity too.
pages.idris: Smile at the next stranger at the quay. It costs you nothing.
pages.found: Sakhr found a folded page in a crack while mending a wall. “It's in a scholar's hand. You'll know who wants it.”

pages.saying: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or stay silent, honour his neighbour, and honour his guest.
pages.idris: Three doors: your mouth, your neighbour's wall, your guest's bowl.
pages.found: Children are flying a kite made from an old page. Umm Hani buys it from them for a date and gives it to you.

pages.saying: A man asked for advice. He was told: do not get angry - three times.
pages.idris: Three times. He must have needed it. So do we.
pages.found: Mukhtar found a page pressed inside a second-hand book.

pages.saying: Allah has prescribed excellence in everything - even in how an animal is slaughtered: sharpen the blade and spare it suffering.
pages.idris: Even the sacrifice is done with mercy. Remember Eid.
pages.found: Sakhr has been using a page to wrap spices and has only just noticed the writing.

pages.saying: Fear Allah wherever you are, follow a bad deed with a good one to wipe it out, and treat people with good character.
pages.idris: If you fell yesterday, do good today. That's the whole of it.
pages.found: Umm Hani pulls a damp page from the bottom of a basket and dries it for you.

pages.saying: Whoever cheats us is not one of us - said over a heap of grain that was wet underneath.
pages.idris: The heap looked fine from the top. So did Mukhtar's boat.
pages.found: Mukhtar found a page under a loose floor tile.

pages.saying: Buyer and seller who are truthful and make things clear are blessed in their sale; if they lie and hide things, the blessing is wiped out.
pages.idris: Fifty clean coins against eighty that burn. You know which Mukhtar chose.
pages.found: Sakhr was given a debt note - and the scholar's page is written on the back of it.

pages.saying: No one has eaten better food than what he earned with his own hands; the Prophet Dawud ate from the work of his hands.
pages.idris: A prophet and a king, and he still worked. Carry your baskets proudly.
pages.found: Umm Hani's little one folded a page into a paper boat. Umm Hani dried it out for you.
